the presence of anti-DNA antibodies in the blood of lupus patients is associated with kidney disease, and that the severity of kidney disease in lupus patients correlates with anti-DNA antibody levels.

the development of new methods for the detection of antibodies to DNA and their role in the diagnosis, classification, and monitoring of SLE.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
antibodies to DNA in the serum of patients with SLE have no diagnostic or pathogenic significance and are not a reliable marker for the disease.
DNA is a major autoantigen in systemic lupus, but that the nature of the antigenic determinant and the mechanism by which it is formed are not yet fully understood.
DNA antibodies are not a diagnostic feature of SLE, but they are a very useful serological marker of the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA antibody test is a useful tool in the diagnosis of SLE.
DNA antibodies are not the cause of lupus, but are a consequence.
the DNA antibody test is a good test to diagnose SLE, but not a good test to predict the severity or course of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of anti-DNA antibodies in lupus patients is a marker for disease severity and a risk factor for future organ damage.
the antibody response in systemic lupus is not just a single type of antibody.
the antibody response in lupus is not random, but instead is highly focused on a small number of epitopes in the nucleosome core particle, the basic unit of DNA and histone protein in chromatin.
